title: Chapter 1 Quiz 5
description: What a program is, the kinds of languages, and how code becomes a running program.
instructions: Take your time: read each question carefully, then check your answer.

questions.question: A computer **program** is best described as…
options: The list of keys the user presses on the keyboard
The algorithm written in a language a computer can run
The physical computer that carries out the algorithm
The algorithm drawn as a flowchart and run by a person
questions.explanation: Programming is the translation of an algorithm into a programming language that the computer can execute.

questions.question: Match each kind of programming to a language used for it.
questions.explanation: Pascal is procedural, C++ is object-oriented, SQL manipulates databases, JavaScript is a scripting language and HTML is a tag language.

questions.question: Which of these languages are normally **compiled**, according to the course?
questions.explanation: The course lists Pascal, C and C++ as compiled languages. Watch out: Python and PHP are interpreted.

questions.question: Which of these languages is normally **interpreted**?
questions.explanation: The course lists Java, Visual Basic, PHP, LISP, PROLOG and Python as interpreted. Watch out: C++ looks like C, but both are compiled.

questions.question: What does a **compiler** do?
options: Translates a whole source program into machine language
Checks the spelling of the data typed by the user
Draws the flowchart of the finished source program
Writes the algorithm for the programmer in plain language
questions.explanation: A compiler is an executable program that translates source code into machine language.

questions.question: An interpreted program can be executed without being fully translated into machine language first.
questions.explanation: Interpreted languages run the program step by step, without translating it all in advance.

questions.question: A source file can be run by the machine directly, with no translation.
questions.explanation: Source files must be translated into machine language, by compilation or by interpretation, before they can be executed. Watch out: the machine does not understand source text.

questions.question: What does **IDE** stand for?
questions.explanation: An IDE is software used to develop programs. Free Pascal and CodeBlocks are examples.

questions.question: A program is written in one or more {{1}} files, which must be translated into {{2}} language before they can be executed.
questions.explanation: Source files are translated into machine language by compilation (or run by interpretation).

questions.question: Which of these are IDEs or SDKs named in the course?
questions.explanation: Free Pascal and CodeBlocks are IDEs. Visual Studio and Android Studio are SDKs. Watch out: JavaScript is a language and machine code is what compilation produces, not development tools.
